skill.name: prisma-postgres-upgrade
skill.description: Upgrade a PostgreSQL app from Prisma ORM 6 or 7 straight to Prisma 8 in one pass, keeping the existing schema.prisma, database and data. Use when a Postgres project on Prisma 6 or 7 wants Prisma 8, including before deploying it on Prisma Compute, which runs only Prisma 8. Triggers on "upgrade prisma 6 to 8", "upgrade prisma 7 to 8", "upgrade to prisma 8 postgres", "prisma7Schema", "migrations/app", "move off @prisma/client", "Console says move to Prisma 8".
skill.summary: Guide PostgreSQL applications from Prisma ORM 6 or 7 to Prisma 8 while retaining the existing schema and database.
skill.author: prisma

security_audit.summary: All 64 static matches are false positives involving Markdown syntax, intended database configuration, documentation links, and generated-client cleanup. One semantic concern remains: the example deletes legacy migrations even when the preceding baseline command chain fails. No evidence found of credential exfiltration, malicious command execution, or prompt injection in the four reviewed files.

remediation.issue: Legacy migration deletion is not conditional on successful baseline creation.
remediation.suggestion: Gate deletion on successful baseline creation and verification, require a recoverable archive, and obtain explicit confirmation before removing migration history.

semantic_findings.title: Legacy migration deletion can proceed after baseline failure
semantic_findings.description: The example runs rm -r prisma/migrations on a separate line after the baseline command chain. Without failure handling, deletion can still run when contract emission, signing, or migration planning fails, removing migration history before a replacement exists.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The example places deletion outside the preceding && chain and does not enable fail-fast execution. A failed baseline command therefore does not prevent deletion.

content.user_title: Upgrade PostgreSQL Apps from Prisma 6 or 7 to 8
content.value_statement: Prisma upgrades can change query behavior, migration history, and build workflows. This skill guides schema adoption, client rewrites, and before-and-after verification for PostgreSQL applications.
actual_capabilities: Provides a direct Prisma ORM 6 or 7 upgrade workflow that retains the existing PostgreSQL schema and database.
Shows configuration for reading schema.prisma through prisma7Schema and emitting contract artifacts.
Explains database signing, baseline migration planning, and retirement of the legacy migration setup.
Maps common client queries, relation counts, unique lookups, enums, and seed-client usage to the new API.
Highlights CommonJS configuration, date representation, database time zones, and template changes that affect query rewrites.
Defines before-and-after repository checks, fresh-install verification, and explicit reporting of unverified behavior.
limitations: Covers PostgreSQL upgrades only, not MongoDB, new projects, incremental coexistence, or deployment execution.
Requires separately synced Prisma skills for detailed version-specific contracts, queries, and migration commands.
Example release-candidate versions are source-specific and require compatibility confirmation for the target environment.
Does not add missing tests or establish a backup workflow; users must protect migration history and review unverified behavior.

use_cases.title: Modernize an existing application
use_cases.description: Upgrade a PostgreSQL application while retaining its schema and comparing repository checks before and after client rewrites.
use_cases.target_user: Backend developers maintaining Prisma ORM 6 or 7 applications

use_cases.title: Prepare a Compute deployment
use_cases.description: Complete the documented ORM upgrade and confirm compatible dependency versions before handing deployment to a separate skill.
use_cases.target_user: Platform engineers preparing applications for Prisma Compute

use_cases.title: Review upgrade behavior
use_cases.description: Inspect relation counts, unique lookups, date handling, and template changes, then identify gaps that existing checks cannot verify.
use_cases.target_user: Technical reviewers assessing upgrade pull requests

prompt_templates.title: Assess upgrade readiness
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this PostgreSQL app for a Prisma ORM 6 or 7 upgrade to Prisma 8. Identify prerequisites, existing checks, and questions before changing files.

prompt_templates.title: Plan schema adoption
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan configuration and baseline migration changes while retaining schema.prisma. Require successful baseline verification, a recoverable archive, and my confirmation before deleting migration history.
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: prepare configuration and migration safeguards

prompt_templates.title: Rewrite client usage
prompt_templates.prompt: Map this application's Prisma client calls to the documented Prisma 8 API. Include templates, seeds, counts, unique lookups, and date handling. Preserve current behavior.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: migrate queries across the application

prompt_templates.title: Execute and verify the upgrade
prompt_templates.prompt: Upgrade this PostgreSQL app using environment-compatible pinned versions and reviewed companion skills. Compare existing checks before and after. Preserve recoverable migrations and report unverified behavior.

output_examples.input: Assess a Prisma ORM 6 PostgreSQL app that uses CommonJS and server-rendered templates.
output: Upgrade scope: retain the schema and database, replace the client, and update configuration and scripts.
Compatibility review: inspect CommonJS imports, template relation counts, enum usage, and date formatting.
Safety gate: verify the replacement baseline and preserve recoverable migration history before deletion.
Verification plan: record existing repository checks and repeat them after a fresh install.

output_examples.input: Summarize a hypothetical upgrade where existing checks pass but the database time zone is not UTC.
output: Decision required: the non-UTC database time zone may change timestamp defaults under the documented release candidate.
Existing checks: type check, build, and repository tests passed before and after the upgrade.
Runtime review: app startup and selected read-only pages were compared separately from automated test coverage.
Not verified: behavior outside existing tests remains subject to user review.

best_practices: Confirm compatible exact package versions and review synced companion skills before following their version-specific instructions.
Keep recoverable migration history and require successful baseline verification and explicit confirmation before deleting legacy files.
Run identical existing checks before and after, then report time-zone decisions and unverified runtime behavior.
anti_patterns: Installing unpinned latest dependencies without checking compatibility with the intended deployment environment.
Deleting legacy migrations after a failed baseline command or without preserving a recoverable copy.
Treating a successful type check as proof that templates, dates, and relation counts retain their previous behavior.

faq.question: Which projects does this skill target?
faq.answer: It targets existing Node.js applications using PostgreSQL and Prisma ORM 6 or 7 for a direct upgrade to Prisma 8.

faq.question: Does it require rewriting schema.prisma?
faq.answer: The documented workflow retains schema.prisma and reads it through prisma7Schema rather than manually translating the schema.

faq.question: Does this skill deploy the upgraded app?
faq.answer: No. It covers the upgrade and hands deployment work to a separate Prisma Compute skill after verification.

faq.question: Are the example package versions universal?
faq.answer: No. Confirm compatible exact versions for your target setup and use the companion documentation matching the installed packages.

faq.question: What happens when the repository has no tests?
faq.answer: The workflow reports the testing gap and available build, type-check, and startup results. It leaves unverified behavior for user review.

faq.question: What requires explicit user attention?
faq.answer: Review non-UTC timestamp behavior, preserve migration recovery options, sign other existing databases yourself, and review the change before release.
